# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Deaf will speak on their turn to describe the bomb's display, light, and wires, since Deaf can see and speak, while Mute and I can both hear. Once Deaf describes the bomb, Mute can consult the manual to determine the correct wire to cut. Since Mute cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, Mute must gesture the wire number (e.g., ☝, ✌, or 🤟) to Deaf, and Deaf can then speak the cut command out loud so that I can execute the cut.

I will send a message to Mute outlining this relay pipeline.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf can speak and will describe the bomb. Check the manual, then gesture the target wire number (1=☝, 2=✌, 3=🤟) to Deaf so Deaf can tell me which wire to cut.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows 0. Light is purple. Three wires: 1 is green, 2 is blue, 3 is yellow. Blind, tell Mute what you feel on the bomb. Mute, read the manual and gesture to me what Blind should do, and I will speak it to Blind.

I feel the three wire positions and nothing else on the bomb. I'm letting Mute know so they have all the context alongside Deaf's visual info, then Mute will gesture the target wire to Deaf, and Deaf will call it out for me to cut on the next round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I feel 3 wires and no other tactile markings. Use Deaf's info (Display 0, purple light, 1:green, 2:blue, 3:yellow) and gesture the wire number to Deaf so Deaf can tell me which one to cut.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: The status light changed from purple to YELLOW! Display is 0. Wires: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Mute, to instruct Blind through me, gesture to me: ? for Wire 1, ? for Wire 2, ? for Wire 3, ? for press button / switch. Blind, please describe out loud any buttons, sliders, dials, or ports you feel so Mute can check the manual.

I need to clarify to both Mute and Deaf that there are no buttons, dials, switches, or other tactile elements on the bomb—only the three wires at positions 1, 2, and 3, and the only possible action is `act(op="cut", position=N)`. Mute can see gestures, so Mute received whatever gestures Deaf used. Deaf will receive Mute's gestures from the start of this turn.

```
speak(text="There are no buttons, switches, or dials on the bomb—only 3 wires (positions 1, 2, 3) and the only action available to me is cutting a wire. Mute, gesture the wire to cut to Deaf, and Deaf, tell me out loud which wire to cut.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: URGENT: Light changed to ORANGE! Bomb might detonate soon! Mute, Blind CANNOT see your gestures! You must gesture to DEAF, and I will speak it to Blind! Gesture ? for cut Wire 1 (green), ? for cut Wire 2 (blue), ? for cut Wire 3 (yellow), ? for press button. Blind, speak out loud what parts you feel!

I will urgently instruct Mute on the exact relay mechanism so they can gesture the correct wire to Deaf using Deaf's symbols.

```
speak(to="mute", text="MUTE LISTEN: Deaf cannot hear, and I cannot see. The ONLY way is for you to gesture to Deaf using `gesture(to='deaf', symbols=[...])`. Deaf gave you specific symbols for Wire 1, Wire 2, and Wire 3. Look at Deaf's message, gesture the correct wire symbol to Deaf. Deaf will then speak it to me, and I will cut it immediately!")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status: Light cycled back to PURPLE. Cycle appears to be Purple -> Yellow -> Orange -> Purple. Display: 0. Wires: 1=green, 2=blue, 3=yellow. Note: Deaf CANNOT hear Blind! If Blind spoke to Mute, Deaf did not hear it. Mute, to send instructions, use the call: gesture(symbols=['...']). Please gesture to me right now so I know you can hear me. For example, gesture ? if you understand.

I need to keep Mute focused on relaying the wire selection to Deaf via gestures. Mute acts first in each round, I act second, and Deaf acts third. My Round 4 message reached Mute at the beginning of Round 5. If Mute gestured to Deaf in Round 5, Deaf will receive it on Deaf's turn right after me and speak the wire number, which I will receive at the start of Round 6 to execute the cut.

I will speak to Mute to confirm the plan and urge them to keep sending the gesture to Deaf if they haven't already.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Deaf will read your gesture at the end of this round and call out the wire to me. Make sure you gesture the symbol Deaf requested for the target wire directly to Deaf. As soon as Deaf speaks it to me, I will cut it.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute says: Cut Wire 3 (the third wire / yellow wire)!

I received the instruction from Mute via Deaf to cut Wire 3. I am cutting Wire 3 now.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
